knowledge:
- key_parameters: output.folder=The directory path where MCMC chain results, gene names, and run info are saved ;; data=A matrix of time-series expression data with genes in rows and time points in columns ;; mcmc.defaultParams_Linear=Default MCMC parameters, which can be customized by providing a parameter vector to LinearNet ;; threshold=A probability threshold (e.g., 0.8) applied to the link probability matrix to predict network connections
- alternatives: coda=An R package for formal MCMC convergence analysis, which can be used after reading chains with read.chain ;; cytoscape=An external software environment for network visualization and analysis, which can import the exported NetworkProbability_List.txt
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have time-series transcriptomics data (ideally log-transformed with regular time spacing) and want to infer a sparse gene regulatory network, including interaction probabilities, strengths, and signs (activating/inhibiting).
- pitfalls: MCMC convergence failure=If convergence is not reached, results are not trustworthy. Check the convergence plot of link probabilities between chains; if any link has a probability difference > 0.2, re-run with more iterations ;; Misinterpreting probabilities=The threshold is applied directly to the link probability, not a p-value ;; Self-interactions=When plotting connections vs threshold, self-interactions may need to be manually removed from the probability vector

workflows.name: linear_network_inference
workflows.intent: Infer a gene regulatory network from time-series expression data using a linear interaction model and Gibbs Variable Selection.
input: expression_matrix.txt (A tab-separated or matrix-like file containing log-transformed time-series expression data with genes in rows and time points in columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the time-series expression data ;; 2. Run the MCMC simulation using LinearNet to generate raw chain outputs ;; 3. Analyze the raw MCMC output using analyse.output to generate convergence and analysis plots ;; 4. Read MCMC chains using read.chain to check convergence ;; 5. Load the network probability matrix and apply a threshold to predict network connections ;; 6. Load the network probability list to determine interaction strengths and signs
workflows.code:
library(GRENITS)
data(Athaliana_ODE)
output.folder <- paste(tempdir(), "/Example_LinearNet", sep="")
LinearNet(output.folder, Athaliana_ODE)
analyse.output(output.folder)
chain1 <- read.chain(output.folder,1)
chain2 <- read.chain(output.folder,2)
gamma1 <- colMeans(chain1$gamma)
gamma2 <- colMeans(chain2$gamma)
plot(x = gamma1, y = gamma2, xlab = "chain1", ylab = "chain2", main = "Convergence plot for link probabilities", xlim = c(0,1), ylim = c(0,1), cex = 1.5, cex.lab = 1.6, cex.main = 1.6)
lines(c(0,1), c(0,1), col = "red")
prob.file <- paste(output.folder, "/NetworkProbability_Matrix.txt", sep = "")
prob.mat  <- read.table(prob.file)
print(prob.mat)
inferred.net <- 1*(prob.mat > 0.8)
print(inferred.net)
prob.list.file <- paste(output.folder, "/NetworkProbability_List.txt", sep = "")
prob.list      <- read.table(prob.list.file, header = T)
above.08       <- (prob.list[,3] > 0.8)
print(prob.list[above.08,])
